notes: Covers the original Call of Duty (2003) dedicated server (CoDMP.exe / cod_lnxded run with +set dedicated 2); the same command dialect carries through the id-Tech-3-derived CoD titles (United Offensive, CoD2, CoD4, World at War), which is why sources for those games agree with the CoD1 ones here. RCON is the Quake 3 connectionless UDP scheme, NOT Valve Source RCON: send a single UDP datagram of 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF followed by 'rcon <password> <command>' to the server's game port (net_port, default 28960) and read the 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF 'print' reply - hence flavour 'custom'. There is no enable switch; RCON is live as soon as rcon_password is set to a non-empty value in the server config (the dvar is written rcon_password, spelled rcon_Password in the anarchyrules dvar list, and the engine treats dvar and command names case-insensitively). In an in-game client console these same commands are typed as '/rcon status' etc.; over the wire only the command text in this file is sent, so no /rcon prefix is recorded. Player identity: kick and ban here take the CLIENT NUMBER (the 'num' column of status, 0..sv_maxclients-1), which is reassigned as players join and leave, so always re-run listPlayers immediately before acting. Name-taking variants exist ('kick <name>', 'banUser <name>', 'tempBanUser <name>') but are unreliable because CoD names carry ^-colour codes that must be typed exactly. The second identifier in the status output is the CD-key GUID (accountId in playerParse); banclient writes that GUID to ban.txt, which is why the ban list is keyed on it. No unban command is recorded: the live command is 'unbanUser <player name>', which takes a name and not the client number (attested by the zeroy wiki, tacodewolff and BigBrotherBot alike), so feeding it a playerId would silently unban nobody - unban by editing ban.txt (lines are 'GUID' or 'GUID Name'; the file sits in main/ next to the server binary on Windows and under the homepath, e.g. ~/.callofduty/main/, on Linux) and restarting, or run unbanUser by hand with the exact name. 'tempBanClient <id>'/'tempBanUser <name>' exist on this engine but take no duration argument (the length is fixed by the engine, ~1 hour), so no {duration} ban form is recorded; BigBrotherBot's CoD parsers likewise fall back to clientkick for temporary bans. Source disagreement, all cosmetic: the zeroy wiki and tacodewolff write the camel-case forms banClient/banUser/tempBanClient/unbanUser while BigBrotherBot's parser sends lowercase banclient/unbanuser; the engine's command lookup is case-insensitive, and lowercase is recorded here because it is what an established admin tool actually sends. gamesclan's CoD1 page lists status, say, map, map_restart, map_rotate, clientkick, banclient and a set of scr_ dvars, omitting the tempban and unban forms that zeroy documents; that is an omission rather than a contradiction. Confidence high: clientkick, banclient, status and say are each attested by at least two independent sources (the zeroy CoD modding wiki, an unrelated hosting knowledgebase at gamesclan, and BigBrotherBot's parser source, whose _commands table sends exactly 'clientkick %(cid)s', 'banclient %(cid)s' and 'say %(message)s'). One caveat on 'serverinfo': it is documented by zeroy and by tacodewolff, but tacodewolff's wording is close to verbatim zeroy, so treat that pair as one lineage - serverinfo is a standard id-Tech-3 console command and is not load-bearing for moderation, which is why the file's confidence is not reduced for it.
